mainTopic: Which parts of the קרבנות hold each other back: the מנחה and נסכים, the blood placements, and the animals of the מוספין. Also, the order of the מנחה and the נסכים.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the earlier discussion of תפילין with a פסוק from ישעיהו about life and healing. A new משנה then teaches that the מנחה (flour and oil) and the נסכים (wine) do not hold each other back. It also teaches that the blood placements on the outer מזבח do not hold each other back. The גמרא brings a ברייתא where the רבנן and רבי disagree about the order of the מנחה and the נסכים. After trying several פסוקים, the גמרא concludes that everyone agrees the מנחה comes first when the two are brought with a זבח. They argue only when the מנחה and נסכים come by themselves. There, רבי puts the נסכים first because the שירה is sung over them. A ברייתא then shows from a פסוק in דברים that one blood placement on the outer מזבח is enough for כפרה. A new משנה teaches that the different animals of the מוספין do not hold each other back, and רבי שמעון prefers one bull with its נסכים over many bulls without them. The גמרא explains that this משנה means the מוספין of ראש חודש and שבועות in ספר במדבר, not those of סוכות, because the תורה says 'כַּמִּשְׁפָּט' about סוכות.

steps.title: Closing verse about those who wear תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the previous discussion with a פסוק from ישעיהו about life and healing.
steps.simpleTranslation: "God is upon them, they will live, and in all of them is the life of my spirit; heal me and make me live."
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the end of the previous topic, not the start of something new. It closes a discussion about the reward for wearing תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ה׳ עליהם' are read as hinting to people who carry God's name on them, meaning in their תפילין. The promise of 'יחיו' and 'החייני' is understood as a blessing of life and healing for them.

keyTerms.meaning: and heal me / make me recover

phrases.english: "The Lord is upon them, they will live,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 38:16. The גמרא is finishing a thought from before: this פסוק is read as being about people who wear תפילין.

phrases.english: and altogether therein is the life of my spirit;
and have me recover, and make me to live."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion of the merit of תפילין.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Wearing תפילין brings a blessing of long life and healing.

steps.title: Flour, oil, wine and blood placements do not depend on each other
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the מנחה (flour and oil) and the wine of the נסכים do not hold each other back. It also rules that the blood placements on the outer מזבח do not hold each other back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The flour and the oil do not prevent the wine, and the wine does not prevent them. The blood placements on the outer altar do not prevent one another.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה gives a rule about pieces of the קרבן service that are not tied together. If one piece is missing, the others still count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many parts of the Temple service are 'מעכב': if one part is missing, the whole thing fails. Here the משנה says the flour-and-oil and the wine are separate, so you can bring one without the other. Likewise, the blood placements on the outer מזבח are not tied to each other. Even if not all were done, the קרבן still works after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: hold back; one part's absence makes the other invalid
placements of blood on the מזבח
the outer altar, in the Temple courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: 'אין מעכבין' does not mean these parts are optional. They are all required. It only means that if one is missing, the others are still valid.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The fine flour and the oil
do not hold back the wine,
phrases.notes: 'Hold back' means that if one is missing, the other still counts and can be brought.

phrases.english: and the wine does not hold them back.
The placements of blood on the outer altar
do not hold back one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: מתני׳ הסולת והשמן אין מעכבין את היין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the closing of the תפילין discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מנחה and the נסכים are independent of each other, and the blood placements on the outer מזבח are independent of each other.

steps.title: Which comes first: meal offering or libations
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings two views. The תנא קמא says the מנחה comes before the נסכים. רבי says the זבח comes and then the נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And their meal offering and their libations': bring the meal offering, and afterward bring the libations. רבי says: 'an animal offering and libations': bring the animal offering, and afterward bring the libations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the order of bringing the מנחה and the נסכים. Each opinion reads the order from the order of words in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא learns from 'ומנחתם ונסכיהם' (במדבר 29:18) that the מנחה is brought before the wine. רבי learns from 'זבח ונסכים' (ויקרא 23:37) that the נסכים come right after the זבח. In his view, the נסכים come before the מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: meal offering of flour and oil
libations; the wine poured on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: The two views disagree on the order in practice. This sets up the question of how רבי explains the פסוק the תנא קמא relies on.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
"And their meal offering and their libations"

phrases.aramaic: הָבֵא מִנְחָה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָבֵא נְסָכִים.
phrases.english: bring the meal offering, and afterward bring the libations.
Rabbi says: "an animal offering and libations"

phrases.aramaic: הָבֵא זֶבַח, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָבֵא נְסָכִים.
phrases.english: bring the animal offering, and afterward bring the libations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the משנה's mention of the flour, oil and wine by discussing their order.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא says the מנחה comes before the נסכים. רבי says the נסכים come right after the זבח.

steps.title: What does רבי do with the other verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the פסוק 'ומנחתם ונסכיהם' puts the מנחה first, so how can רבי disagree?
steps.simpleTranslation: But for רבי too, isn't it written, 'And their meal offering and their libations'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי's view. The פסוק the תנא קמא used is in the תורה for רבי too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of words in 'ומנחתם ונסכיהם' seems to say clearly that the מנחה comes first. The question is how רבי can say the נסכים come before the מנחה, against that פסוק.

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi also,
isn't it written: "And their meal offering and their libations"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי's opinion from the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's view that the נסכים come before the מנחה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק 'ומנחתם ונסכיהם' puts the מנחה first, which seems to go against רבי.

steps.title: רבי uses the verse for a different lesson
steps.stepSummary: רבי uses 'ומנחתם ונסכיהם' to teach that the מנחה and נסכים may be brought at night, or even the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק is needed to teach 'their meal offering and their libations' even at night, and 'their meal offering and their libations' even the next day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי. He does not use that פסוק for order at all; he uses it to teach about timing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the פסוק is busy teaching a different lesson, it cannot also teach the order. The lesson is that once the animal was brought during the day, its מנחה and נסכים are not tied to that time. They may be brought at night, or even on the next day.
steps.whatToRemember: Don't hold on to this answer. Step 8 shows that the רבנן also need the teaching about night and the next day, so it cannot explain the argument. Steps 11 and 12 give the final explanation.

phrases.english: That verse is necessary for "their meal offering and their libations" at night,
phrases.notes: He means that even if the animal was brought by day, its מנחה and נסכים can still be brought at night.

phrases.english: and "their meal offering and their libations" even the next day.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the פסוק to a different lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ומנחתם ונסכיהם' seemed to teach the order, with the מנחה first.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי, the פסוק teaches that the מנחה and נסכים may be brought at night or the next day, not the order.

steps.title: Doesn't the פסוק 'זבח ונסכים' support רבי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the רבנן. The פסוק 'זבח ונסכים' puts the נסכים right after the זבח, which sounds like רבי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן too: isn't it written 'an animal offering, and libations'?
steps.whatsHappening: Step 4 challenged רבי from a פסוק. Now the גמרא challenges the רבנן from a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the words 'זבח ונסכים' place the נסכים straight after the זבח. That matches רבי's order: זבח, then נסכים. So how can the רבנן say the מנחה comes before the נסכים?

keyTerms.meaning: Wine poured on the מזבח together with a קרבן
But isn't it written? (an opening for a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis too,
isn't it written: "An animal offering, and libations"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It mirrors the challenge of Step 4, this time aimed at the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's ruling that the מנחה comes before the נסכים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The order of words in the פסוק ('זבח ונסכים') puts the נסכים right after the זבח, against the רבנן.

steps.title: The רבנן use 'זבח ונסכים' for זעירי's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן need the פסוק to teach that the נסכים become fixed in holiness only when the זבח is slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק is needed for זעירי's teaching. זעירי said: the נסכים become fixed in holiness only through the slaughter of the זבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for the רבנן. They use 'זבח ונסכים' to teach something else, not the order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the נסכים to the זבח. זעירי reads that link as being about holiness, not order. The נסכים become fully tied to the animal only once it is slaughtered. Since the פסוק is used up on this teaching, it says nothing about order.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)

phrases.english: That verse is needed for the teaching of Ze'eiri,
as Ze'eiri says:
Libations do not become consecrated
except through the slaughter of the animal offering.
phrases.notes: Once the animal is slaughtered, its נסכים are locked to it and can't be moved to another קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers Step 6 by giving the פסוק a different job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirecting the פסוק to a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'זבח ונסכים' teaches the order of the נסכים.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'זבח ונסכים' teaches זעירי's rule about when the נסכים become holy.

steps.title: Both sides need both פסוקים, so neither one proves order
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבי also needs זעירי's teaching. The רבנן also need the teaching about bringing at night and the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי also needs that פסוק for זעירי's teaching. And the רבנן also need 'ומנחתם ונסכיהם' to teach that the מנחה and נסכים may be brought at night, and even the next day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down both explanations so far. Each side needs both פסוקים for other teachings, so neither פסוק can be the source for the argument about order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said רבי uses 'ומנחתם ונסכיהם' for night and the next day. Step 7 said the רבנן use 'זבח ונסכים' for זעירי. But surely both sides accept both teachings. Then both פסוקים are used up for everyone, and we still don't know where the argument about order comes from.

phrases.english: But Rabbi too needs it for the teaching of Ze'eiri,
and the Rabbis too need
"their meal offering and their libations" for bringing them at night,
and "their meal offering and their libations" for bringing them even the next day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It undoes the answers of Step 5 and Step 7 together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both teachings are accepted by both sides, then neither פסוק is free to teach order, so the argument has no source.

steps.title: A new source for the רבנן: 'עולה ומנחה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the רבנן learn their order from the words 'עולה ומנחה', which put the מנחה right after the קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is the reason of the רבנן: it is written 'a burnt offering and a meal offering'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts over and gives the רבנן a different פסוק as their source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'עולה ומנחה' place the מנחה straight after the animal. That means the מנחה comes before the נסכים, which is the רבנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
An offering of flour and oil

phrases.english: Rather, this is the reason of the Rabbis,
as it is written: "A burnt offering, and a meal offering"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 8 knocked out the earlier sources, this offers a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new פסוק as the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument depends on 'זבח ונסכים' and 'ומנחתם ונסכיהם'.

steps.title: But רבי also has the פסוק 'עולה ומנחה'
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק is in front of רבי too, so how can he disagree?
steps.simpleTranslation: But for רבי too, isn't it written 'a burnt offering and a meal offering'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer. רבי must also accept this פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'עולה ומנחה' clearly puts the מנחה first, רבי cannot ignore it. So it seems רבי should agree with the רבנן.

phrases.english: But for Rabbi too, isn't it written: "A burnt offering, and a meal offering"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It challenges the source offered in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that 'עולה ומנחה' is the source of the argument
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק both sides must accept cannot explain why they disagree.

steps.title: Everyone agrees when there is a זבח; they argue only when the מנחה and נסכים come alone
steps.stepSummary: When the מנחה and נסכים come with a זבח, everyone puts the מנחה first because of 'עולה ומנחה'. They argue only when the two are brought by themselves. The רבנן learn that case from the case with a זבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: when they come with a זבח, everyone agrees that the מנחה comes first and then the נסכים, because it is written 'עולה ומנחה'. They argue when the מנחה and נסכים are brought by themselves. The רבנן hold: since with a זבח it is מנחה then נסכים, by themselves it is also מנחה then נסכים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes what the argument is about. It is no longer about the case with a זבח. It is about a מנחה and נסכים brought on their own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עולה ומנחה' settles the case where the מנחה and נסכים come with a זבח, and everyone agrees. The argument moves to the case where they come alone. The רבנן copy the order from the case with a זבח: מנחה first. The next step gives רבי's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Brought together with an animal offering

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that with a זבח, the מנחה comes before the נסכים. They argue only about a מנחה and נסכים brought on their own. The רבנן say the same order applies there too.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא in Step 3 sounded like a general argument about order. Now the גמרא limits it to a מנחה and נסכים brought on their own. In the usual case, with a זבח, there is no argument at all.

phrases.english: Rather, with regard to those that come with the animal offering,
everyone agrees
that the meal offering comes and afterward the libations,
since it is written: "A burnt offering, and a meal offering."
Where they disagree is about those brought by themselves,
phrases.notes: He means a מנחה and נסכים brought without any animal offering.

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold:
Since when they come with the animal offering,
it is the meal offering and afterward the libations,
by themselves too
it is the meal offering and afterward the libations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, בְּבָאִים עִם הַזֶּבַח דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers Step 10 by limiting the argument to a different case.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the order in the usual case: with a זבח, the מנחה comes before the נסכים, according to everyone.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing which case the argument is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument is about the מנחה and נסכים that come with a זבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: With a זבח everyone agrees. The argument is only about a מנחה and נסכים brought by themselves, and the רבנן learn that case from the case with a זבח.

steps.title: Why רבי puts the libations first when they come alone
steps.stepSummary: רבי agrees that the מנחה comes first when there is a זבח, because the altar finishes its 'eating' first. When the מנחה and נסכים come by themselves, the נסכים are more important because the שירה is sung over them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי holds: only there, with a זבח, since the altar started 'eating', it finishes all the eating first. But when they come by themselves, the נסכים are more important, because the שירה is sung over them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי can agree with the case of 'עולה ומנחה' and still argue about a מנחה and נסכים brought by themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a זבח, the altar starts by 'eating' the animal, so it keeps going with the מנחה, which is also eaten. Pouring wine is more like drinking, so it waits. Without a זבח there is no eating already going on, so the נסכים go first because the לויים sing the שירה over them.

keyTerms.meaning: since already, because it already started
eating, here the altar 'eating' the burned offerings
the song the לויים sing during the offering

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that with a זבח the מנחה comes first. רבי says that by themselves the נסכים come first because of the שירה. The רבנן learn the case without a זבח from the case with a זבח.

phrases.english: And Rabbi holds: it is specifically there
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case where the מנחה and נסכים come together with a זבח.

phrases.english: that since it already began with eating
it finishes the whole matter of eating
phrases.notes: Burning the מנחה counts as 'eating' too, while pouring wine is more like drinking.

phrases.english: but when they are by themselves, the libations are preferable
since the song is said over them

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי, הָתָם הוּא דְּאַיְּידֵי דְּאַתְחֵיל בַּאֲכִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from Step 11 by giving רבי's side: why the 'עולה ומנחה' case does not carry over to a מנחה and נסכים brought by themselves.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between cases (with a זבח vs. without)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since 'עולה ומנחה' puts the מנחה first, רבי should agree that the מנחה always comes first.
steps.terutzMaskana: The order with a זבח comes from the altar finishing its 'eating'. Without a זבח, the נסכים take priority because of the שירה.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: outer altar blood placements do not hold each other back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line in the משנה that the blood placements on the outer altar do not hold each other back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The placements of blood on the outer altar do not hold each other back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה. It quotes it to set up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many קרבנות need two or four placements of blood on the outer altar. The משנה says that if some were missed, the קרבן still works after the fact. The next step shows where this comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: placements of blood on the altar
the outer altar, in the courtyard
hold back, prevent the מצוה from working

phrases.english: The placements of blood on the outer altar
do not hold each other back.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּתָּנוֹת שֶׁעַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן אֵין מְעַכְּבוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The discussion of the order of מנחה and נסכים is finished, and the גמרא returns to another line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Missing some of the blood placements on the outer altar does not stop the קרבן from working after the fact.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives the פסוק: one placement is enough
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that for every קרבן whose blood goes on the outer altar, one placement is enough for כפרה. It learns this from the פסוק 'וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Where do we learn that for all offerings whose blood goes on the outer altar, if one put the blood on with one placement, it brought כפרה? From the פסוק: 'And the blood of your offerings shall be poured out on the altar of ה׳ your God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the source for the משנה's rule from Step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about the blood of all 'your offerings' and uses one act of pouring. This shows that one placement is enough after the fact, even for a קרבן that normally needs two or four placements.

keyTerms.meaning: it brought atonement; the קרבן worked

steps.whyThisMatters: It means a קרבן is not ruined if the כהן did only one placement instead of the full number.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: From where do we learn
regarding all offerings whose blood is placed on the outer altar
that if one placed them with one placement, it effected atonement?
As it is stated:
"And the blood of your offerings shall be poured out
on the altar of the Lord your God."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן לְכׇל הַנִּיתָּנִין עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source from the פסוק for the משנה's rule quoted in Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's rule that the outer altar placements do not hold each other back.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the פסוק 'וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ עַל מִזְבַּח ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ'.

steps.title: New משנה: the festival animals do not hold each other back
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that the bulls, rams, sheep and goats of the מוספין do not hold each other back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The bulls, the rams, the sheep and the goats do not hold each other back.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that if one kind of animal from the festival מוספין is missing, the others can still be brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On festivals, several kinds of animals are brought as the מוסף. The משנה says each one stands on its own, so missing one kind does not cancel the rest.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The bulls and the rams
and the sheep and the goats
do not hold each other back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה opens a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The different animals of the festival מוספין do not hold each other back.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: one bull with libations is better than many without
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says that if there is money for many bulls but not for their נסכים, they should bring one bull with its נסכים, and not all the bulls without נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: If they had many bulls but did not have נסכים, they should bring one bull with its נסכים, and they should not bring all of them without נסכים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון adds a rule to the משנה for a case where there is not enough for all the נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think it is best to bring as many bulls as possible. רבי שמעון says a bull with its proper נסכים is better than many bulls missing their נסכים, so they should bring only one bull, done fully.

keyTerms.meaning: wine libations that go with a קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not saying the נסכים hold back the bull. He is only saying which choice is better when there is not enough for everything.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
If they had many bulls,
but they did not have libations,
phrases.notes: He means they did not have enough money for the נסכים of all the bulls.

phrases.english: one should bring one bull and its libations,
and they should not sacrifice all of them without libations.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אִם הָיוּ לָהֶם פָּרִים מְרוּבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רבי שמעון's view to the משנה's rule from Step 15, for a case where there are not enough נסכים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If there are not enough נסכים for all the bulls, bring one bull with its נסכים rather than all the bulls without נסכים.

steps.title: Which holiday's bulls and sheep does the משנה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking which holiday's מוספין the משנה is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: These bulls and sheep, which holiday are they from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the new משנה by asking a simple question: which holiday's bulls and sheep does the משנה have in mind? This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will try out an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the animals of the מוספין do not hold each other back. Different holidays have different מוספין, so the גמרא needs to know which one the משנה is describing before it can understand the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? Which case is this?

phrases.english: GEMARA: These bulls and sheep, from where are they?
phrases.notes: He means: which holiday's מוספין is the משנה talking about? The rams are included too, even though only bulls and sheep are named.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה quoted in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which holiday's מוספין the משנה is describing.

steps.title: It cannot mean the offerings of סוכות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests סוכות, but rejects it because the תורה says those offerings must be brought 'כַּמִּשְׁפָּט'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means the offerings of the חג (סוכות), that is a problem, because 'כַּמִּשְׁפָּט' and 'כְּמִשְׁפָּטָם' are written about them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible answer, the offerings of סוכות, and right away shows why it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כַּמִּשְׁפָּט' and 'כְּמִשְׁפָּטָם' mean 'according to the rule', so the offerings must be brought exactly as written. If one part is missing, the whole thing is not done right. That clashes with the משנה's rule that the animals do not hold each other back.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means the holiday of סוכות
According to the rule. It shows the offering must be done exactly as written
According to their rule. Same idea as כַּמִּשְׁפָּט
If you say. It introduces a suggestion the גמרא is about to reject

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the bulls of סוכות are not real מוספין. They are. It is only saying the משנה's rule (that the animals do not hold each other back) cannot apply to them, because the תורה demands they be brought exactly as written.

phrases.english: If you say they are those of the festival,
phrases.notes: חַג here means סוכות, with its many bulls.

phrases.english: 'According to the rule' and 'according to their rule' are written about them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question of step 17 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that the משנה is talking about the מוספין of סוכות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוקים for סוכות say 'כַּמִּשְׁפָּט' and 'כְּמִשְׁפָּטָם', which means each part holds the others back. That contradicts the משנה's rule.

steps.title: It means ראש חודש and שבועות in ספר במדבר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the משנה means the מוספין of ראש חודש and שבועות listed in ספר במדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means the offerings of ראש חודש and עצרת (שבועות) from חומש הפקודים (ספר במדבר).
steps.whatsHappening: Since סוכות does not work, the גמרא answers that the משנה must mean the מוספין of ראש חודש and שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not write 'כַּמִּשְׁפָּט' about these offerings, so the animals can be offered without each other. The גמרא points to the list in ספר במדבר: two bulls, one ram and seven sheep.

keyTerms.meaning: The start of a new month
The name the משנה and גמרא use for שבועות
The 'Book of the Countings', meaning ספר במדבר

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule that the מוספין animals do not hold each other back is about ראש חודש and שבועות. It is not about סוכות, because the תורה says 'כַּמִּשְׁפָּט' there.

phrases.english: Rather, those of the New Moon and Shavuot
phrases.notes: עֲצֶרֶת is what the גמרא usually calls שבועות.

phrases.english: of the book of Numbers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ וַעֲצֶרֶת דְּחוֹמֶשׁ הַפְּקוּדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting סוכות in step 18, it gives the correct answer to step 17's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה refers to the מוספין of ראש חודש and שבועות as listed in ספר במדבר.
